questiontext.text: Which practice best demonstrates least privilege?

answer.text: Grant only the access needed for the task and limit its scope and duration
Give every user administrator access to reduce delays
Use the root account for all daily work
Disable account authentication

questiontext.text: Which statement distinguishes authentication from authorization?

answer.text: Authentication establishes identity; authorization determines permitted actions
Authentication assigns file permissions; authorization encrypts files
They are two names for package installation
Authorization establishes identity; authentication decides file ownership

questiontext.text: What is defense in depth?

answer.text: Using multiple security controls so one failure does not defeat all protection
Using one complex password for every account
Replacing backups with a firewall
Running every application as root

false

questiontext.text: What does sudo -l do?

answer.text: Lists commands the current user may run through sudo under the active policy
Lists every installed package and upgrades them
Starts a root shell
Lists network listeners and changes firewall rules

questiontext.text: sudo -l runs each command listed in the user's sudo policy.

answer.text: true
false

questiontext.text: Why is a persistent root shell risky for routine work?

answer.text: Later commands run with broad privilege, increasing the impact of mistakes
It prevents commands from being logged
It automatically disables file permissions
It makes package repositories untrusted

questiontext.text: Why is downloading a script and piping it directly into sudo bash high risk?

answer.text: Downloaded content receives elevated authority before the user inspects and verifies it
It always creates a backup first
It only works on read-only files
It prevents the script from accessing the network

answer.text: The current account's user and group identity information
Installed package signatures
Firewall rules
SSH server host keys

questiontext.text: What does groups report?

answer.text: Groups associated with the current user
All listening network sockets
Groups of installed packages
Users currently connected over SSH

false

answer.text: Installed/candidate versions and package sources known to APT

It changes the user's group membership
It opens the package's network ports

answer.text: Packages with upgrades indicated by the local package metadata
It upgrades all packages immediately
It adds an unknown repository
It lists current SSH sessions only

false

answer.text: It adds another software source whose packages and signing keys may be trusted by the system

It guarantees every package is malicious
It removes the need for updates

questiontext.text: Which set of facts helps determine whether a listening service is reachable remotely?

answer.text: Bind address, routing, host/network firewall policy, and other access controls

questiontext.text: How should a user treat a private SSH key?

answer.text: Keep it secret and protected; do not share or upload it
Post it publicly so servers can verify it
Send it to classmates when they need access
Use it as the server's host key

answer.text: The identity of the remote server
The local user's group membership
The package's version number
The host firewall's default rule

questiontext.text: SSH warns that a known server's host key has changed. What is the safest next step?

answer.text: Stop and verify the new fingerprint with the system owner through a separate trusted channel

Delete the stored key and accept the new one immediately
Share the private key with the server administrator

answer.text: Filter network traffic according to configured rules
Replace software updates and account security
Guarantee every running service is safe
Encrypt every file on the computer

answer.text: true
false

questiontext.text: Which property is important for a useful backup?

answer.text: It is restorable and protected from the same failure as the original
It is stored only on the same disk as the original
It is never tested
It is accessible to every account without controls

questiontext.text: A student suspects a shared computer account was compromised. What should they do?

answer.text: Promptly report it and follow the organization's recovery process
Delete system logs to protect privacy
Install an unverified cleanup tool

answer.text: Identify, inspect, authorize, change, verify, document

Authorize, skip inspection, run as root, assume success
